The failing test is related to the `testUltimateSoftBreak` method and it failed on the assertion that compares the expected and actual output of the `qpcodec.encode(plain)` call.
The assertion error indicates that the expected output contains an encoded soft break sequence `=\r\n` and a tab character encoded as `=09`, but the actual output has the tab character `\t` directly instead of `=\r\nt=09`.

The failure suggests that the encoding of the quoted-printable string is not inserting the soft break correctly.

The likely relevant method for this encoding behavior is the `encode` method of the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class. There are two `encode` methods accepting a `String`: `.encode(java.lang.String)` and `.encode(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)`. It's more likely that the test calls `.encode(java.lang.String)` since there is no charset argument in the test.
